calls.head: The Blues like Suter’s line against Glass’s
calls.body: At home, the Blues keep sending Suter’s line (Toropchenko, Suter and Dvorský) out against opponents’ fourth lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jim Montgomery keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Devils’ fourth line is Boqvist, Glass and Hämeenaho.

calls.head: The Devils’ power play outclasses the Blues’
calls.body: On the power play, New Jersey is one of the league’s best, but St. Louis is near the bottom. Every penalty the Blues take could cost them. These two rarely give each other power plays, so special teams may not get much of a say.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Five points for Neighbours as the Blues beat the Devils
paras: The Blues scored four times in the first. Brandon Carlo scored his first goal for St. Louis just under two minutes in to open the scoring, and the goal stood after the Devils challenged for goalie interference. Jimmy Snuggerud extended the lead to 2-0 on the power play 22 seconds later, and Robert Thomas made it 3-0 less than four minutes later. Jesper Boqvist got the Devils on the board less than three minutes later. Philip Broberg stretched the lead to 4-1, 48 seconds later. New Jersey pulled Connor Hellebuyck after four goals and turned to Jake Allen for the rest of the first. Timo Meier cut St. Louis’ lead to 4-2 late in the first. Luke Hughes pulled the Devils within one on the power play a minute and a half later. The second period was a wild one. Pavel Buchnevich made it 5-3 for the Blues early in the period, but Connor Brown cut it to 5-4, 47 seconds later. Logan Mailloux pushed the lead to 6-4 just under three minutes later. Mason McTavish made it 7-4 on the power play a little over a minute later. It was a busy third period. Jonatan Berggren made it 8-4 early in the period, but Evan Rodrigues cut St. Louis’ lead to 8-5 less than three minutes later. Declan Chisholm made it 8-6 with a little over three minutes left. Berggren scored again into the empty net with a little over two minutes left. Jake Neighbours finished with five assists, and Thomas had a goal and two assists.

The score flatters the Blues: the Devils had the better of the chances. Replay those chances a hundred times and the Devils win about six in ten. Jordan Binnington, who gave up six goals against Anaheim in his last start, made 37 saves for the Blues. The Blues improved to 12-9-2 and climbed to sixth in the Central, while the Devils fell to 15-8-0, second in the Metropolitan.

items.text: Three straight wins for the Blues.
Timo Meier scored again against St. Louis, and has six goals in seven games against them since 2023-24.
Timo Meier has a point in four straight games, with a goal in each of the last three.
Jesper Bratt’s nine-game point streak ended.
